record.original_question: Let (ξ− , ξ+ ) be a pair of (co)oriented contact structures with opposite signs on M , and assume that their contact invariants pair to 1: (2.10) ⟨c(ξ− ), c(ξ+ )⟩ = 1. Does M admit a Reebless foliation?

evidence.quote: Question 2.9. Let (ξ− , ξ+ ) be a pair of (co)oriented contact structures with opposite signs on M , and assume that their contact invariants pair to 1: (2.10) ⟨c(ξ− ), c(ξ+ )⟩ = 1. Does M admit a Reebless foliation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed, oriented 3-manifold. A cooriented contact structure $\xi$ on $M$ is a cooriented 2-plane field given as the kernel of a 1-form $\alpha$ with $\alpha\wedge d\alpha\neq 0$; we say $\xi$ is positive if $\alpha\wedge d\alpha>0$ and negative otherwise. To each cooriented contact structure $\xi$ on $M$ one associates its Heegaard Floer contact invariant: if $\xi$ is positive, $c(\xi)\in\widehat{HF}(-M)$, and if $\xi$ is negative, $c(\xi)\in\widehat{HF}(M)$. There is a natural pairing
$$\langle\,\cdot\,,\,\cdot\,\rangle:\widehat{HF}(M)\otimes\widehat{HF}(-M)\longrightarrow \mathbb{F}_2.$$
A codimension-one foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $M$ is called Reebless if it contains no Reeb component, i.e., no embedded solid torus whose boundary is a leaf and whose interior is foliated as a Reeb component.

Suppose $\xi_-$ and $\xi_+$ are cooriented contact structures on $M$ with $\xi_-$ negative and $\xi_+$ positive, whose contact invariants satisfy
$$\langle c(\xi_-),\, c(\xi_+)\rangle = 1.$$
Question: must $M$ admit a Reebless foliation?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published resolution of this specific question relating a nontrivial pairing of contact invariants of opposite-sign contact structures to the existence of a Reebless foliation on a closed 3-manifold. Related results connect tightness of contact pairs and proximity to Reebless foliations, but the precise question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Surveys in Differential Geometry XXV: Foliations, contact structures and their interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing relations between contact invariants, tightness, and Reebless/taut foliations on 3-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys related results but does not record a resolution of the precise pairing-equals-1 question.

status_evidence.title: Contact perturbations of Reebless foliations are universally tight
status_evidence.snippet: Contact structures sufficiently close to a Reebless foliation are universally tight.
status_evidence.claim: Provides one direction (foliation to tight contact) but not the converse implication asked here.
